sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Ibadat Khana (1575)**: Established at Fatehpur Sikri to facilitate theological debates between Sunni Ulema, later expanded to include Shias, Hindus, Jains, Christians, and Zoroastrians.
• **Shift in Policy**: Transition from **Shariat-centric** governance to **Sulh-i-kul** (Absolute Peace), emphasizing the ruler as a mediator rather than a sectarian leader.
• **The Mahzar (1579)**: A document signed by leading Ulema declaring Akbar the 'Imam-i-Adil' (Just Ruler), granting him the final authority to interpret religious law in case of conflicting opinions.
• **Key Metric**: The decline of the influence of the **Sadr-us-Sudur** (Chief Justice/Religious head) and the rise of the Emperor as the supreme arbiter.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Exclusively Sunni Ulema debates; led to disillusionment due to sectarian bickering.
Search for truth within Islamic orthodoxy.
Inclusion of non-Muslims (Jesuits, Jains, Parsis); debates became broader and philosophical.
Realization that no single religion held the absolute truth.

items.definition: The policy of 'universal peace' or 'absolute peace' that formed the bedrock of Akbar's religious tolerance, aiming to harmonize diverse religious communities.
Often called the 'Infallibility Decree', it empowered Akbar to choose between conflicting interpretations of the Sharia, effectively curbing the power of the orthodox Ulema.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Jesuit Missions**: Three missions invited from Goa to Fatehpur Sikri to explain Christianity.
• **Jain Influence**: Hiravijaya Suri was invited to the court, leading to the prohibition of animal slaughter during certain periods.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Intense opposition from orthodox Ulema (e.g., Mulla Abdullah Sultanpuri) and the 1580 rebellion in Bengal/Bihar.
• **Solutions**: Consolidation of the 'Din-i-Ilahi' (1582) as a moral code to unify the nobility.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'I-M-S' (Ibadat, Mahzar, Sulh-i-kul).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Ibadat Khana (1575) -> Mahzar (1579) -> Sulh-i-kul (Policy outcome).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often claims the Mahzar made Akbar 'infallible' in all matters. Correction: It only gave him the right to choose between conflicting interpretations of the Sharia, not to create new laws contrary to the Quran.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Eclecticism' to describe Akbar's approach. Quote: 'Akbar's religious policy was not a rejection of Islam, but a re-interpretation of it in an Indian context.'

keyTakeaways: The Ibadat Khana was the laboratory for Akbar's religious synthesis.
The Mahzar was a political tool to subordinate the Ulema to the state.
The shift from 1573-1580 represents the maturation of Mughal administrative secularism.
